intro.title: Why I'm Here
intro.quote: Poetry teaches us to choose every word with devotion and care, and invites us to listen to them with tenderness and awe. In this simple act, we find the purest foundation of love.
intro.body:
This is my space to express myself as I've fallen in love with poetry.

It's a form of therapy. It gives me breath while taking my breath away. It's where my love lives. It's where I can be understood. It's where I grow.

My Infinite Adore, when your heart is ready, you'll know where to find me.

analyses.title: Forever — is composed of Nows —
analyses.author: Emily Dickinson
analyses.excerpt:
Forever — is composed of Nows —
'Tis not a different time —
Except for Infiniteness —
And Latitude of Home —
analyses.fullText:
Forever — is composed of Nows —
'Tis not a different time —
Except for Infiniteness —
And Latitude of Home —

From this — experienced Here —
Remove the Dates — to These —
Let Months dissolve in Further Months —
And Years — exhale in Years —

Without Debate — or Pause —
Or Celebrated Days —
No different Our Years would be
From Anno Dominies —
analyses.analysis:
I return to this poem the way some people return to prayer—with the kind of reverence that makes my breath stutter and my chest warm all at once. Every time I read it, I feel a physical shift in me, as if something in my ribs catches fire while another part of me drops into a sudden, crystalline stillness. It's not an abstract poem to me. It’s a lived, bodily experience. It's magic, right here.

Dickinson does something I can barely articulate: she collapses eternity into the present moment so completely that I feel the world sharpen around me. My heart pulls tight, like it’s being opened from the inside. There’s heat. There’s cold. There’s the strange sensation that time just… unstitches itself.

When she writes that *forever* isn't somewhere else, not later, not after death, but here—right here—I feel the truth of it in my chest. It's the same heat I get when I'm in love, when I’m paying attention, when life becomes so bright and present that I forget to check the clock. Eternity arrives quietly, in the now. In breath. In presence.

Years ago, I engraved this line—“Forever is composed of Nows”—on my favourite watch. It was a vow to myself before I even fully understood it. A vow to be intentional with my energy, my love, my time. A vow to notice. To listen. To be amazed by the small things that create the now.

And now, rereading this poem, I see what I failed to understand back then: all of her words, all of this insistence on the present, circles back to **love**. Love as attention. Love as devotion. Love as presence strong enough to stretch a single moment into infinity.

She dismantles time in such a sensual way—stripping away the dates, the calendars, the "celebrated days"—and what’s left is not emptiness but the raw moment itself, bare and shimmering. Reading it, I feel something almost holy: this idea that if we lived with that kind of awareness, our years would be indistinguishable from God’s own. Isn't this magical?!

When I sit with this poem, I feel myself dissolve into the truth she’s uncovering: that forever is not a place we go, but a way of being here. And every time I feel my chest warm, every time a moment of love makes me forget the shape of time, I understand her a little more.

This poem doesn’t just speak to me—it rearranges me.

originals.title: My Infinite Adore
originals.text:
My Infinite Adore
I lay each stone in silence
a dwelling untouched
For when your heart remembers
our unwritten pages
The walls will wake
to whisper the version of us
time was too young to hold

originals.title: Rubberband
originals.text:
I got this rubberband on my wrist
and i snap it every time that i think about your lips
I got this rubberband on my wrist
almost break it every time that i'm trying to forget
I got this rubberband on my wrist
and i snap it every time to remember you exist
I got this rubberband on my wrist
and I break it every time I remember the promise I still haven't kept yet

originals.title: Through your eyes
originals.text:
Do you still see the ghost I used to be?
Or do I wear his shadow on my skin?
Am I forever tethered to his memory?
Or can you see where I begin?

I've shed the past like borrowed sin,
do you still mistake the ashes for the flame?
As I rise, untouched by him,
will I be someone you love again?

originals.title: Grilled Cheese
originals.text:
I'm Noah, eyes always wet, waiting for the door to open.
But the house I'm building isn't wood or paint.
It's the four walls, the roof, and the door of my heart.
Untouched by the scars.

And the soft breath I'm left with in your absence,
barely enough to keep me alive,
feeds the light on the front porch.

So when that knob finally turns,
you can sit at the table,
and I'll make you a grilled cheese.
